title: Add synthetic prompt generator + prompt-shape buckets (seedable workload profiles)
author: Rina Kobayashi
description: Summary: This PR adds a synthetic prompt-shape generator and a seedable workload profile so perf-canary runs are reproducible across regions/hosts and can be tuned without touching code. The goal is to approximate production request shapes (prefill/decode mix, prompt length buckets) without using any customer prompts or identifiers. Why: Baselines and regression detection require stable distributions. Early canary scaffolding used a fixed prompt and random lengths, which made p95 latency and tokens/sec variance too high and made comparisons across runtime versions noisy. What’s included: 1) PromptShape + WorkloadProfile config types (YAML) with explicit length buckets and weights; 2) Seeded RNG for selecting shapes, generation params, and per-run determinism; 3) A small library that produces “prompt skeletons” (shape only) that can be filled by a static, non-sensitive text corpus shipped with the service; 4) Guardrails to prevent accidental generation of unique/high-cardinality prompts (bounded vocabulary + truncation + stable templates). Non-goals: This does not attempt to match semantic content, tool-calling schemas, or customer-specific formatting. This is intentionally shape-only for privacy and stability. Follow-ups: Add a control-plane surface for selecting profiles per model/region, and tune weights based on aggregated production histograms (without collecting prompts).
commits: perf-canary: add seedable RNG + deterministic selection of buckets
perf-canary: add default profile v0 + unit tests for determinism
perf-canary: wire profile selection into request loop
docs: document buckets/weights and how to reproduce a run
notable_snippets: configs/workload_profiles/default-v0.yaml: buckets: [{name: "xs", prompt_tokens: [32,128], max_new_tokens: [64,128], weight: 0.34}, {name: "s", prompt_tokens: [128,512], max_new_tokens: [128,256], weight: 0.33}, {name: "m", prompt_tokens: [512,2048], max_new_tokens: [128,512], weight: 0.23}, {name: "l", prompt_tokens: [2048,4096], max_new_tokens: [256,768], weight: 0.10}] prefill_decode_mix: {mode: "target_output_tokens", target_output_tokens: 256}

internal/workload/profile.go: type WorkloadProfile struct { Name string; Seed int64; Buckets []PromptBucket; TemperatureRange [2]float64; TopPRange [2]float64; StopSequences []string; MaxConcurrent int; }

internal/workload/prompt_shape.go: func (g *Generator) NextShape() (PromptShape, error) { bucket := g.pickBucketWeighted(); promptLen := g.rng.Intn(bucket.PromptMax-bucket.PromptMin+1) + bucket.PromptMin; maxNew := g.rng.Intn(bucket.NewMax-bucket.NewMin+1) + bucket.NewMin; return PromptShape{Bucket: bucket.Name, PromptTokens: promptLen, MaxNewTokens: maxNew, Temperature: g.pickFloat(bucket.TempMin, bucket.TempMax), TopP: g.pickFloat(bucket.TopPMin, bucket.TopPMax)}, nil }
testing: Unit: internal/workload/profile_test.go covers deterministic shape generation given a fixed seed and verifies bucket weights converge within tolerance over 50k samples. Unit: prompt_shape_test.go validates bounds (min/max tokens, max_new_tokens) and that no generated prompt exceeds configured byte limits after template fill + truncation. Manual: ran perf-canary locally against staging endpoint with --print-shapes to confirm stable output across repeated runs and that tokenization estimates track actual tokenizer counts within expected error.
ci_checks: build (linux/amd64): pass; unit-tests: pass; lint (golangci-lint): pass; config-validate: pass
rollout_plan: No production rollout by itself. This is a library/config change. perf-canary service will consume default-v0 profile in the next deployment PR. For baseline runs, we will pin seed and profile in the Helm values to ensure identical distributions across runtime versions.
privacy_and_safety_notes: This generator does not ingest or emit customer prompts. Prompt bodies are assembled from a fixed static corpus and templates (checked into repo) and then truncated to the target token budget. The selection is deterministic under a seed to avoid accidental uniqueness/cardinality blowups. No per-request IDs or prompt text is added to metrics/logs; only shape labels (bucket name) are exposed. Bucket name set is finite and controlled by config validation.
review_conversation: Noah Patel (review): Can we guarantee the seed affects everything (bucket pick, lengths, temperature/top_p) and not rely on math/rand global state? Also please confirm default buckets reflect typical production request shapes (not just long-context). Rina Kobayashi (author): Yep — generator owns a private RNG instance; removed any global rand usage. Default-v0 is biased toward short/medium prompts; added long-context-v0 as an opt-in profile. Added docs + tests proving determinism and bounds. Sofia Ivanova (review): I’m slightly worried about bucket labels as a new metric dimension. Are we going to include bucket in metrics by default? If yes, ensure it doesn’t explode cardinality. Rina Kobayashi (author): Bucket is a fixed small enum (xs/s/m/l). We only emit bucket in debug logs for now; metrics label wiring remains in PR-19212. Added config validation to enforce <= 12 buckets and alphanumeric names. Logan Wright (review): Please add a hard cap on filled prompt bytes before tokenization, and a test that it never exceeds the cap. Also add a note that corpus/templates are non-sensitive. Rina Kobayashi (author): Added MaxPromptBytes=24KB cap + truncation before tokenization, plus a unit test for worst-case template fill. Updated docs with explicit note on corpus/templates being static and shipped with the service. Logan Wright (review): Looks good. Approved.
decision_notes: Chose seedable deterministic selection to reduce variance in baseline/regression comparisons; chose shape-only prompts (static corpus + templates) to avoid any coupling to customer content; kept the bucket set configurable via YAML to allow tuning per model/region without code changes.
